  "summary": "This two-page Maharashtra Government Gazette document presents L. C. Bill No. XIV of 1984, circulated on 11 July 1985 to elicit public opinion. The bill proposes civil and criminal immunity for physicians and surgeons who withdraw life-sustaining treatment from patients suffering from terminal illness. It defines medical treatment, patient, petitioner, physician, surgeon, and terminal illness, and sets out procedures for withdrawal of treatment when a mentally competent patient makes a written request and the physician or surgeon is satisfied that the patient has a terminal illness or terminal injury.",
  "The bill also provides that compliance with the withdrawal request would protect the physician, surgeon, patient, and the patient’s family from civil or criminal liability. It establishes court petition procedures where a hospital or physician does not act on the patient’s request, and includes a model Declaration and Draft Special Power of Attorney. These forms allow a person of sound mind to refuse artificial medical treatment, request that resuscitation cease after cardiac arrest, and appoint attorneys to act when the person can no longer make decisions. The document is an institutional legislative draft rather than an authored argument, and the pages shown contain no record of the bill’s subsequent enactment or legislative outcome.",
